# T009.1 — Rewrite Login as a Razor Page

## Summary

The independent ASP.NET Core host now serves the Descope client-side login page at `/login.aspx`. The unchanged .NET Framework application remains in the solution.

## Changes (files and why)

- `DescopeSampleApp.Core/Program.cs` — Register and map Razor Pages alongside the existing MVC and API endpoints.
- `DescopeSampleApp.Core/Pages/Login.cshtml` — Recreate the login form, pinned CDN scripts, web component, success/error event handlers and navigation as a layout-free Razor Page. Razor's escaped `@@` renders literal `@` in CDN URLs. The success target is `/AuthenticatedPage.aspx` as explicitly requested for this task, rather than the legacy page's `/`.
- `DescopeSampleApp.IntegrationTests/LoginPageTests.cs` — Offline WebApplicationFactory GET tests for the characterized login URL and case variant, rendered content type, pinned CDN URLs, component configuration, form, event handlers and success target. The test client never fetches external CDN scripts.

## Decisions (rationale and sources)

- Keep the side-by-side rewrite; no legacy source, deployment, CI, IIS or proxy change. Source: approved plan T009 and run scope; ASP.NET Core Razor Pages documentation, `https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/razor-pages/?view=aspnetcore-10.0`.
- Keep the client-side Descope flow without introducing server authentication or migrating unrelated legacy assets. The WebForms `runat="server"` attribute is not meaningful on the Razor form; its visible form ID and component are preserved. Source: unchanged `DescopeSampleApp/Login.aspx`, empty `Login.aspx.cs`, and T002.1 source characterization.
- The requested `/AuthenticatedPage.aspx` success navigation intentionally differs from the legacy `window.location.replace('/')`; T010 still owns serving that destination in the new host. The login page does not assert a server redirect or a completed sign-in.

## Validation (commands and results)

- `msbuild -restore -p:RestorePackagesConfig=true -p:Configuration=Release -m -nologo -v:minimal` — PASS (exit 0); existing legacy NU1902 jQuery advisory and MSB3247 binding-conflict warnings remain.
- `dotnet test --no-build -c Release` — PASS (exit 0); 76 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (23 net48 characterization; 53 net10 integration).
- Lint — none defined.

## Follow-ups and risks

- Browser execution of the CDN scripts, Descope web component, event delivery and resulting client navigation is unverified by offline HTTP tests. CDN availability is not tested.
- `/AuthenticatedPage.aspx` on the new host is planned for T010; no server-side session or authentication is claimed.
